players.bio: Michigan's 2026 Mr. Basketball and the Michigan Sports Writers' Division 1 player of the year. Led East Lansing to CAAC Blue, district and regional titles and the Division 1 state final as a senior. Signed with Bowling Green. players.about:
The 2026 Hal Schram Mr. Basketball, Torbert and his father, Kelvin Torbert (2001, Flint Northwestern), are the first father and son to both win the award. He was also the Michigan Sports Writers' 2026 Division 1 Player of the Year, the Lansing State Journal's Player of the Year in 2024-25 and 2025-26, a four-time all-state pick (including AP Division 1 first team in 2023-24 and the Free Press all-class Dream Team as a senior) and all-conference all four seasons.

He played his freshman season (2022-23) at Okemos, where the team went 18-5, before transferring to East Lansing. In his three seasons there the Trojans went 79-6, won three CAAC Blue titles, three district titles, three regional titles and the 2024-25 Division 1 state championship, and reached the Division 1 state final in 2025-26. As a senior he averaged 25.0 points, 6.0 rebounds and 2.7 steals, and he finished his career with 2,009 points.

moments.title: 24 points and the defensive assignment
moments.text: Torbert scored a game-high 24 points, with two open-court dunks, and set up four 3-pointers by Kellen Lott and Tyree Anthony. Defensively he took the lead on Brother Rice star Jordan McDaniel, who scored 14 in the first half and three in the second as East Lansing turned a one-point halftime lead into a 62-41 win, its 31st straight.

moments.src: MLive (Patrick Nothaft), Jan. 11, 2026: "KJ Torbert's 39 points lead top-ranked East Lansing past No. 2 Rockford"
moments.title: 39 points in a No. 1 vs. No. 2 overtime win
moments.text: In front of more than 2,000 fans, Torbert scored 39 points, with five 3-pointers, as top-ranked East Lansing beat No. 2 Rockford. After Rockford rallied from 10 down to take a 67-65 lead, his floater tied it with 10 seconds left, and he stole the ball near half court for a last-second layup try at the regulation buzzer. Then he scored East Lansing's first eight points of overtime to pull away.
moments.quote: I've been built for moments like that

moments.src: Lansing State Journal (Brian Calloway), Feb. 6, 2026: "KJ Torbert adds to Mr. Basketball candidacy, helps East Lansing top Waverly"
moments.title: 39 points and a buzzer-beater from near half court
moments.text: With Kingston Thomas out injured, Torbert scored 39 points with eight rebounds at Waverly. He tied the game at halftime with a 3 from just inside half court at the buzzer, then scored 17 in the fourth quarter as a 53-48 lead became a 17-point win. It was East Lansing's 40th straight win and gave the Trojans a two-game lead in the CAAC Blue.
moments.quote: To me he's hands down Mr. Basketball

moments.src: Lansing State Journal (Brian Calloway), Feb. 27, 2026: "East Lansing boys basketball adds to district title streak with win over Waverly"
moments.title: 30 points for a sixth straight district title
moments.text: Torbert scored 30 points with four steals as East Lansing built a 51-24 halftime lead on eight first-half 3-pointers and beat rival Waverly for the third time that season, winning the program's sixth straight district title.

moments.src: Lansing State Journal (Brian Calloway), March 5, 2026: "KJ Torbert, Kingston Thomas power East Lansing basketball to regional title"
moments.title: 15-point third quarter breaks it open
moments.text: After Kingston Thomas got East Lansing the halftime lead, Torbert took over with 15 points in the third quarter by attacking the basket. He finished with 28 points and six rebounds as the Trojans won their fourth straight Division 1 regional title.

moments.title: Mr. Basketball, like his father
moments.text: Torbert was named Michigan's Mr. Basketball with 3,625 points in the voting, well ahead of runner-up Cameron Ryans of Grand Rapids Northview (1,962). He and his father, Kelvin Torbert (Flint Northwestern, 2001), became the first father and son to win the award, and he was the fourth Greater Lansing winner and the first since Waverly's Marcus Taylor in 2000. He had led the area in regular-season scoring at 25.8 points a game, with 6.2 rebounds, 2.7 steals and 58 3-pointers.

Lansing State Journal (Brian Calloway), March 10, 2026: "East Lansing basketball takes another big step in quest for title repeat"
moments.title: 17 first-half points to take control
moments.text: Torbert scored 17 of his team-high 24 points in the first half, when East Lansing hit five 3-pointers in a 25-12 second quarter to take control. He added six assists and four rebounds as the Trojans reached the Breslin for the second straight season.

moments.src: Lansing State Journal (Nathaniel Bott), March 13, 2026: "KJ Torbert delivers 3 in final seconds, sends East Lansing to title game"
moments.title: Step-back 3 sends East Lansing to the final
moments.text: With the game tied 52-52 in the closing seconds, Torbert hit a step-back 3-pointer with under two seconds left to put the Trojans in the Division 1 final. He scored 24 points, 11 of them in the third quarter after a quiet first half, and with East Lansing down 45-40 late he set up Tyree Anthony's corner 3, then drove for the basket that tied it at 45.
moments.quote: This is the stuff you dream of

moments.src: Lansing State Journal (Brian Calloway), March 14, 2026: "East Lansing boys basketball denied in bid for repeat in D1 state final"
moments.title: 28 points in his final game
moments.text: In his last high school game, Torbert scored a game-high 28 points and tied the Division 1 final at 50 with a 3-pointer late in the fourth quarter. Rockford doubled him the rest of the way. Afterward he said he expected East Lansing to be back at the Breslin the next season.

players.about:
Sexton's career scoring leader with 1,967 points, Summerville was all-conference all four seasons (2022-23 to 2025-26). As a senior he was all-state in Division 2, named to BCAM's Best and the Michigan Sports Writers' first team. The Lansing State Journal named him all-area as a freshman and sophomore and to its Dream Team as a junior and senior.

In his four seasons the Big Reds went 72-24 and won 2 league titles, 2 district titles and a regional title. He averaged 19.8 points as a junior, with 46 3-pointers and 76% free-throw shooting, and 21.7 points as a senior, when Sexton won the CAAC White and a district title.

When Michigan Center called a timeout it didn't have with 0.3 seconds left, he made both technical free throws to seal the win and send Sexton to the regional final.

His senior class won the CAAC White title and back-to-back district titles and reached back-to-back regional finals, and coach Deleon Dearing credited the group with bringing a spark back to the school and the program.

players.about:
Johns was the 2017 AP Class A Player of the Year and all-state all four seasons, including AP first team in 2016, 2017 and 2018 and the Free Press and Detroit News Dream Teams as a senior, when he was also named to BCAM's Best of the Best. He was all-conference all four years, the Lansing State Journal's Player of the Year in 2016, 2017 and 2018, runner-up for the 2018 Hal Schram Mr. Basketball (2,792 points) and No. 60 in ESPN's national top 100.

In his four seasons (2014-15 to 2017-18), the Trojans went 81-15. They went unbeaten in the regular season in 2015-16 (23-1) and 2016-17 (24-1), winning the CAAC Blue and a district title both years, then won district and regional titles in 2017-18 (22-4) before a 58-55 state quarterfinal loss to West Ottawa. As a senior he averaged 26.0 points and 10.1 rebounds, finishing with more than 1,800 career points.

He played four seasons at Michigan (2018-19 to 2021-22), reaching three Sweet 16s and the 2021 Elite Eight, then spent his graduate season at VCU (2022-23).

At Oakland (2009-13) he became the program's winningest player, part of teams that won 87 games and reached two NCAA Tournaments. He then spent two seasons as a graduate manager under Tom Izzo at Michigan State (including the 2015 Final Four), two as an Oakland assistant (2015-17) and four on Porter Moser's staff at Loyola Chicago (2017-21), where he ran the defense: the Ramblers reached the 2018 Final Four and the 2021 Sweet 16, and the 2020-21 team led the nation in scoring defense.

Named Loyola's head coach in 2021 at 30, the youngest in Division I, he won 25 games and the Missouri Valley tournament title in his first season and took the Ramblers to the NCAA Tournament. In 2023-24 they went 23-10 and shared the Atlantic 10 regular-season title; in 2024-25 they went 25-12 and reached the NIT semifinals. moments.text: Murray was part of the senior class that won the CAAC White title and back-to-back district titles, reached back-to-back regional finals and went 23-3 in its final season. Coach Deleon Dearing credited the group with bringing a spark back to the school and the program.

moments.src: Lansing State Journal (Nathaniel Bott), Feb. 25, 2026: "Waverly thumps Grand Ledge, sets up showdown with East Lansing"
moments.title: Filling the stat sheet against Grand Ledge
moments.text: Ali had 15 points, eight assists, seven rebounds and five steals as Waverly beat Grand Ledge 97-71 to reach the district final.
